annotations.text:
Neon Green on black in all four, with the app's own derived tones (wash = accent at 15%, rules = dim at 59%), so structure is the only variable. The lateral pinned pane stays in every one.

All four are drawable in GDI: flat fills, 1px rules, text, blitted thumbnails. Terminal is the only one that needs no icon work at all.

TERMINAL — leading candidate

Axis: identity.

Commits to the 5250 heritage the neon palette comes from. Character-grid columns, hard edges, no radii, inverse-video selection, and a function-key legend along the bottom instead of a cramped hint strip — which is also the honest fix for discoverability. A command-line prompt replaces the boxed search field. 17 rows.

Tradeoff: it is a strong period style. If you ever want clip2 to look contemporary rather than deliberately retro, this is the hardest direction to walk back.

COLUMNS

Axis: density.

Splits the main list into two columns: 34 items on screen against today's 12, with no reduction in row height or type size.

Tradeoff: each item gets about 210px of content width, so anything longer than a short path or identifier truncates. Best if you mostly recognise items by their first few words.

SECTIONS

Axis: information architecture.

Groups the list by recency — Last hour / Today / Earlier — so you scan a band rather than a flat 47-item list. The row design barely changes; what changes is how you find things.

Tradeoff: headers cost roughly three rows of space, and grouping only earns that back once history is genuinely old and varied. Useless on a short list.

EXPAND

Axis: depth.

The selected item opens in place as a panel showing the whole thing plus its actions — the preview pane's benefit without spending a third column on it. Multi-line content stops being one clipped line.

Tradeoff: the open panel costs about four rows, and the list shifts under you as you arrow through it. The closest of the four to what is already built.
